intent: To inform viewers about the proportion of people who consider themselves 'cat people'.

units.meaning: People who describe themselves as "cat people" make up 11.5% of the measured population.

basis.note: Table value is 11.5; unit is percent.

accepted_routes: 11.5% of people consider themselves cat people.
Cat people are 11.5% of the total.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The numeric label for the cat-people data point must read 11.5% or 11.5 percent.
units.temporal_anchor: The single narration clause stating 'Only 11.5% of people consider themselves cat people.'
units.reviewer_question: Must the video display the exact numeric value 11.5%, or is an unlabeled segment insufficient?

optional_valid: Using the word 'only' as emphasis for the 11.5% share.
Showing the donut chart's remaining area as unlabeled context.
Using a donut chart to convey part-to-whole composition.
unsupported_to_avoid: 88.5% are dog people; the complement is not cat people, not necessarily dog people.
Cat ownership rates or numbers of cats.
Causal claims about why 11.5% consider themselves cat people.
Extrapolating to a different population or future time.
Comparing to dog people without another table row.
notes: Only one table row supports the cat-people share: 11.5% (relative 0.1150). The main risk is treating the complement as dog people or confusing self-identified cat people with cat owners.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only

trim.reason: 人工逐条指定：删除/合并
